title: Liquidity & the Fed
headline_read: Liquidity is ample — no monetary squeeze in sight.

indicators.title: M2 Money Supply · year-over-year
indicators.context: How fast the broad money supply is growing versus a year ago. Double-digit growth (2020-21) preceded the inflation surge; the 2022-23 contraction was the first since the Great Depression.
indicators.read: M2 is growing 5.6% a year — a normal pace.

indicators.title: Fed Balance Sheet · total assets
indicators.context: Everything the Federal Reserve holds, in trillions. Rising means the Fed is injecting liquidity (QE); falling means it's draining (QT) — the tide that lifts or lowers all markets.
indicators.read: The Fed's balance sheet is little changed from a year ago, now $6.72 trillion.
indicators.no_severity_reason: A descriptive level of the monetary plumbing — this lens's verdict is carried by M2 money-supply growth.

indicators.title: Bank Reserves at the Fed
indicators.context: Cash banks park at the Fed — the system's core liquidity buffer. When QT drains reserves too low, funding markets seize up (as in September 2019).
indicators.read: The level of bank reserves is down 12% from a year ago, now $2.97 trillion.
indicators.no_severity_reason: A descriptive level of the monetary plumbing — this lens's verdict is carried by M2 money-supply growth.

indicators.title: Overnight Reverse Repo
indicators.context: Spare cash money-market funds park at the Fed overnight. It acts as the system's overflow tank: a high balance means excess liquidity; near zero means the buffer is spent and QT bites reserves directly.
indicators.read: The overnight reverse-repo facility is down 98% from a year ago, now $3.3 billion.
indicators.no_severity_reason: A descriptive level of the monetary plumbing — this lens's verdict is carried by M2 money-supply growth.
